subject: Reserved capacity scenario modeling and discount gate
messages:
From: Lauren Meyers <lauren@eunoiahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@eunoiahealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity sizing & GPU price sensitivity for rollout

Hi Kimberly / Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Eunoia is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. We're trying to shape our procurement ask for a Q4 production rollout and have a few concrete questions before we get to a formal RFP: 

- For a baseline production footprint (~120k requests/day, 1.2k concurrent sessions, average prompt+response 650 tokens), what recommended reserved GPU capacity would you size for 12/24/36-month commits?
- How sensitive are discounts to GPU market pricing (e.g., if spot/wholesale GPU costs change by +/-20%)? Do you offer a pass-through or indexation clause?
- What approval path do you typically require for discounts beyond standard tiered schedules? Need to know whether this is an AE/Revenue Ops decision or needs VP/Finance sign-off.

I've attached a short RFP summary that includes traffic shapes and SLA expectations (Eunoia_RFP.pdf). Procurement is especially asking about the risk-sharing constructs if GPU prices spike mid-term.

Would you be able to sketch scenarios this week? We can schedule a brief call with procurement if that's easier.

Best,
Lauren Meyers
Head of Platform Partnerships
Eunoia Health

Attachment: Eunoia_RFP.pdf (application/pdf, 244KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Meyers <lauren@eunoiahealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity sizing & GPU price sensitivity for rollout

Hi Lauren — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP.

Quick answer up-front: we can support your target request volumes with a Dedicated pool sized in the 6–10x GPU range depending on concurrency and batching tolerance. We prepared an initial scenario model and attached it here (reserved_capacity_model.xlsx). It lays out three commit tenors (12/24/36 mos) and three sizing buckets (base, steady-state, burst).

Key summary points (more detail in the model):
- 12-month: lowest commitment flexibility; higher unit price; recommend ~6 GPUs weighted for aggressive batching.
- 24-month: best balance for cost predictability vs. ramp risk; recommend ~8 GPUs; we can offer a tiered 8% discount off list for a 24-mo baseline with performance SLAs.
- 36-month: deepest discount potential (12–15% off list) but requires clear ramp milestones and quarterly usage reviews.

On GPU pricing sensitivity: we typically do not do raw pass-through to customers but we do offer an indexation clause that triggers a limited price protection window if market GPU costs rise >15% year-over-year. For downside (GPU prices drop), we commit to a quarterly rebate mechanism tied to observed effective cost-per-token across similar fleets.

Discount approvals: standard tiered discounts (up to 8%) can be approved by Sales Ops + Regional Rev Manager. Anything beyond 8% or non-standard contract constructs (indexation buybacks, escrowed credits) require Finance/GP sign-off (Marcus) and VP Sales review.

Next steps: I'll loop Marcus and Rachel to confirm the approval ladder and get a recommended starting discount budget and delegate sign-off levels. Would you share preferred procurement timelines?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: reserved_capacity_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 67KB)

Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Eunoia — discount gate & approval matrix (draft)

Team — pulling internal next steps together after Lauren's ask. Quick TL;DR then details below.

TL;DR: recommend we present Eunoia with three options (12/24/36 mo) and an approval gate structure: up to 8% discount allowed by Revenue Ops; 8–14% requires Finance review; >14% needs VP Sales + CFO sign-off. Include a market-index clause that caps Redwood exposure to a 6-month sliding window.

Details / rationale:
- Sizing assumptions: their RFP numbers map to ~0.9–1.1 p99 response latency with a Dedicated pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs assuming continuous batching and 60% sustained utilization. That gives comfortable headroom for burst and model upgrades.
- Discount budget: Eunoia signals enterprise procurement sophistication — likely push for 10–12% at 24mo. Recommend we start with a 8% standard offer and reserve a 10% exec-level concession as negotiation buffer.
- Market risk clause: propose an indexation trigger if vendor GPU input costs (our weighted GPU procurement price) increase >15% over a trailing 6-month median. If triggered, we offer a temporary credit/deferral option: either (a) a one-time credit to offset increased ops for next quarter, or (b) a phased rate rebase with customer consent. This keeps long-term contracts viable without immediate pass-through.
- Approval path: Rachel please prepare a short memo that lists exact approvers and contract language for the finance clause. Marcus: can you confirm whether we have a discretionary discount pool for Q3 deals and the approval SLA?

Attachments: I'm drafting a suggested term sheet (approved_discount_terms_v1.docx) with the three-option structure for external sharing once we align internally.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity sizing & GPU price sensitivity for rollout

Hi Lauren — looping back with a concrete set of options and the next step. Thanks for the clear RFP.

Summary offer (high level):
- Option A (12 mo): 6 A100-e GPUs, unit rate = $0.95/compute-hour, no market-index clause, no rebate mechanism, standard 30-day SLA credits.
- Option B (24 mo): 8 A100-e GPUs, unit rate = $0.88/compute-hour (8% discount), includes quarterly rebate if our realized fleet GPU cost drops >10% vs. baseline, and an indexation guard that we can invoke if our GPU input costs increase >15% (6-month sliding review).
- Option C (36 mo): 8–10 A100-e GPUs (phased activation), unit rate = $0.78/compute-hour (12% discount initial), quarterly ramp checkpoints, and an escrowed credit of up to 3% per year as protection against extreme market swings.

Approval & timeline:
- We can present Option B as standard for a 24-mo ask. Discounts beyond 8% require Marcus (Finance) sign-off. Marcus, Rachel and Kimberly are on copy to finalize the term language; we aim to get a signed term sheet within two weeks if procurement is responsive.

Next steps for Eunoia: please confirm (a) preferred option (A/B/C), (b) procurement contact and target signature date, and (c) whether you want the indexation clause drafted as an optional addendum or embedded in the main SOW. Once you confirm, I'll drop a HubSpot quote (HS-239482) and send a prefilled DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
